notes: The circuit image shows the breadboard with rows j-f at the top and e-a at the bottom; this was mapped to the catalogue naming (bank 'b' = rows f-j at the top of the image, bank 't' = rows a-e at the bottom).

Each LED anode (longer leg, bent left) is in the same column as its resistor; the cathode is in the next column. A black jumper links the cathode column to the top negative rail (tn), and one black wire runs from Arduino GND (next to AREF) to that rail.

Resistors straddle the centre gap: lead 1 in bank 'b' row f, lead 2 in bank 't' row e. Blue signal wires go from the resistor column (row d, bank t) to pins 6, 5, 4, 3 and 2 in turn. Resistor value 220 ohm per the tutorial.
Exact rail hole numbers (tn.2, tn.11, tn.14, tn.17, tn.20, tn.23) are approximate; the whole rail is one strip.
Used GND.1 for the GND header pin beside AREF.
A USB cable connects the board to the computer, as the tutorial requires for serial input. It has no ports in the catalogue, so the edge is not port-specific.
